rounds.text: Thangamayil Jewellery is delivering exceptional financial performance, highlighted by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 83% [E17] and a staggering 264% increase in compounded profit over the same period [E21]. The company’s capital efficiency is elite, with an ROE of 28.1% [E13] and an ROCE of 25.5% [E12] that dwarf the sector benchmarks of 8.16% and 9.66% respectively [E9, E10]. This fundamental strength is attracting significant institutional interest, with foreign holdings rising from 0.25% to 5.54% [E42] and domestic institutional holdings increasing to 16.43% [E43]. Future growth is anchored by management's plan to nearly double the top line within four years [E82], supported by a recent 17.46% increase in retail space [E80] and a target to reach 40 lakh customers by March 2026 [E83]. Conceded: The business commands a high valuation with a P/E of 41.4 [E1] and a P/B of 11.49x [E2], while promoter holdings have declined by 5.55 percentage points since September 2023 [E41]. However, the company’s perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E51] and a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 [E66] suggest the market is responding to its consistent ability to outperform sector median profit and sales growth [E76, E77].

Thangamayil Jewellery trades at a significant valuation premium that the underlying fundamentals may not justify, evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 11.66x which is more than five times the sector benchmark of 2.12x [E7, E63]. This rich valuation is further highlighted by a P/E of 42.22x against a sector average of 27.73x, leaving the stock with a negative margin of safety of -2.2% relative to its intrinsic value [E6, E46]. While the company has shown strong historical performance, the current market price is "price-led," with five-year share price growth of 58% significantly outstripping profit growth of 32% [E56]. Operational risks are emerging as quarterly operating margins have declined by 1 percentage point year-over-year [E31], and there are concerns the company may be capitalizing interest costs [E64]. Furthermore, promoter holdings have decreased by 5.55 percentage points since September 2023 [E41, E65], while total borrowings have climbed to Rs 913 Cr as of March 2026 [E39]. Conceded: the company has delivered exceptional trailing twelve-month profit growth of 264% [E21] and maintains a high return on equity of 28.1% [E13]. However, investors must weigh these gains against a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -66.3% and signals that earnings growth is beginning to decelerate [E53, E71].

Conceded: the price-to-book ratio stands at an elevated 11.66x against a sector benchmark of 2.12x [E7]. However, this premium valuation is fully backed by elite operational returns, with an ROE of 28.1% and ROCE of 23.03% that vastly outshine sector benchmarks of 8.16% and 9.66% respectively [E9, E10, E13]. While the bear points to a negative margin of safety and a price-led setup [E46, E56], trailing twelve-month profit growth of 264% completely eclipses that narrative by proving fundamental earnings power is accelerating far beyond historical averages [E21]. The concern regarding rising borrowings to Rs 913 Cr is counterbalanced by robust operating cash flow of Rs 322 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 249 Cr, demonstrating strong internal cash generation [E35, E36, E39]. Although quarterly operating margins contracted slightly by 1 percentage point [E31], the broader annual trend shows operating margins expanding from 6% to 7% [E30], supported by institutional accumulation with foreign and domestic holdings rising significantly [E42, E43]. Finally, the reduction in promoter holdings [E41] is offset by a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 and a rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 flashing a medium-confidence buy [E51, E66].

Conceded: ROE is 28.1% and ROCE is 23.03% [E9, E10, E13]. However, citing these high returns as justification ignores the severe multiple penalty already levied, where P/B sits at an expensive 11.66x against a 2.12x sector benchmark and EV/EBITDA reaches 27.35x against 14.85x [E7, E11]. Conceded: TTM profit growth hit 264% [E21]. Yet this spike obscures an inconsistent operating margin trend alongside a recent quarterly contraction down to 5% and a warning that earnings growth is decelerating [E31, E33, E71]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 322 Cr [E35]. This generation still coincides with borrowings swelling to Rs 913 Cr and a specific flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E39, E64]. Conceded: institutional holdings increased [E42, E43]. Nevertheless, promoters have reduced their stake by 5.55 percentage points, a sustained insider exit during a price-led rally that trades at a negative margin of safety [E41, E46, E56, E65].

Conceded: P/B is 11.66x and EV/EBITDA is 27.35x [E7, E11], but these multiples reflect a business whose superior efficiency—demonstrated by an ROA of 10.24% against a sector benchmark of 3.41%—fully justifies a quality premium [E8]. Conceded: operating margins showed a recent quarterly dip [E31], but this is typical for a CYCLICAL profile and is heavily outweighed by an operational acceleration where TTM sales grew 83% and TTM profit surged 264% [E17, E21, E58]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 913 Cr [E39], but this expansion directly supports robust fundamentals, yielding ₹322 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹249 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36]. Conceded: promoter holdings decreased by 5.55 percentage points [E41], but institutional investors have aggressively stepped into that vacuum, with foreign holdings increasing and domestic institutions expanding their stake to 16.43%, driving positive institutional money flow [E42, E43, E44].

Conceded: the company generated ₹322 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹249 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36]. However, the bull's justification of high multiples ignores the reality that borrowings climbed to ₹913 Cr in March 2026 from ₹797 Cr previously [E39], alongside a flagged negative warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E64]. Furthermore, while the bull dismisses margin volatility as mere cyclicality [E58], quarterly operating margins actually contracted by one percentage point year-over-year in June 2026, and the overall yearly and quarterly margin trends both read as inconsistent [E31, E32, E33]. The bull highlights surging institutional participation [E42, E43], but this influx coincides with a direct dilution of promoter commitment, with insider holdings dropping by 5.55 percentage points down to 61.61% [E41]. Finally, pointing to strong top-line momentum [E17, E21] sidesteps the reverse DCF reality that the current price already bakes in an aggressive 18.3% earnings growth rate [E47], leaving a negative margin of safety of -2.2% [E46].
